Import External Annotations or Bridge Raw Texts to Corpus Annotations

lexdiv_import_annotations.Rd

lexdiv_import_annotations() aligns complete external token surfaces (including Japanese morphological analyses) with original segment text. lexdiv_as_annotations() bridges raw texts or lexdiv_tokenization objects directly into sealed lexdiv_annotations objects ready for lexdiv_concordance, lexdiv_collocations, lexdiv_keyness, lexdiv_ambiguity_review, and lexdiv_family_profile.

Usage

lexdiv_import_annotations(data, segments, provenance, max_tokens = 1e6)

lexdiv_as_annotations(
  documents,
  texts = NULL,
  id_col = "document_id",
  text_col = "text",
  normalization = "NFC",
  case = "lower",
  keep_numbers = FALSE,
  tokenizer = "english",
  language = "en",
  max_tokens = 1e6
)

# S3 method for class 'lexdiv_annotations'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

Data frame or tibble with character document_id, segment_id, surface, and consecutive positive token_index covering all non-whitespace text in each segment.

segments

Data frame or tibble with unique document_id/segment_id pairs and UTF-8 text.

provenance

Named list of scalar strings including language, analyzer, analyzer_version, dictionary, dictionary_version, unit, and normalization.

documents

For lexdiv_as_annotations(), a named character vector, a data frame/tibble with id_col and text_col, a single lexdiv_tokenization, or a named list of lexdiv_tokenization objects.

texts

Original raw texts required only when documents supplies lexdiv_tokenization objects (verified via source_text_sha256).

id_col, text_col

Column selectors for data-frame inputs.

normalization, case, keep_numbers, tokenizer

Preprocessing parameters used when documents supplies raw texts directly.

language

Language code recorded in provenance.

max_tokens

Positive whole-number ceiling on total token rows.

x

A lexdiv_annotations object.

...

Additional arguments passed to print.data.frame().

Value

A sealed lexdiv_annotations object containing tokens, segments, documents, provenance, and integrity_sha256 (used to verify that aligned source records remain unmodified). When created by lexdiv_as_annotations(), tokens includes is_word (TRUE for lexical words, FALSE for punctuation/excluded spans) and term (normalized/cased word form or NA_character_). print() displays up to 12 token rows and returns x invisibly.

See also

lexdiv_concordance, lexdiv_keyness, lexdiv_tokenize

Examples

# Direct 1-line bridge from raw English texts:
ann <- lexdiv_as_annotations(c(
  d1 = "Hello, world! Cats chase dogs.",
  d2 = "Dogs bark loudly."
))
ann
#> <lexdiv_annotations: 2 documents; 2 segments; 12 tokens; analyzer ldfreq-english-word-tokenizer>
#>  document_id segment_id token_index surface   term is_word is_number start end
#>           d1         s1           1   Hello  hello    TRUE     FALSE     1   5
#>           d1         s1           2       ,   <NA>   FALSE     FALSE     6   6
#>           d1         s1           3   world  world    TRUE     FALSE     8  12
#>           d1         s1           4       !   <NA>   FALSE     FALSE    13  13
#>           d1         s1           5    Cats   cats    TRUE     FALSE    15  18
#>           d1         s1           6   chase  chase    TRUE     FALSE    20  24
#>           d1         s1           7    dogs   dogs    TRUE     FALSE    26  29
#>           d1         s1           8       .   <NA>   FALSE     FALSE    30  30
#>           d2         s1           1    Dogs   dogs    TRUE     FALSE     1   4
#>           d2         s1           2    bark   bark    TRUE     FALSE     6   9
#>           d2         s1           3  loudly loudly    TRUE     FALSE    11  16
#>           d2         s1           4       .   <NA>   FALSE     FALSE    17  17

# External morphological annotation import:
segments <- data.frame(document_id = "ja", segment_id = "s1",
  text = "\u732b\u304c\u6765\u305f\u3002")
tokens <- data.frame(document_id = "ja", segment_id = "s1", token_index = 1:5,
  surface = c("\u732b", "\u304c", "\u6765", "\u305f", "\u3002"))
x <- lexdiv_import_annotations(tokens, segments, list(
  language = "ja", analyzer = "authored", analyzer_version = "1",
  dictionary = "none", dictionary_version = "not-applicable",
  unit = "authored-example", normalization = "none"))
x
#> <lexdiv_annotations: 1 document; 1 segment; 5 tokens; analyzer authored>
#>  document_id segment_id token_index surface start end
#>           ja         s1           1      猫     1   1
#>           ja         s1           2      が     2   2
#>           ja         s1           3      来     3   3
#>           ja         s1           4      た     4   4
#>           ja         s1           5      。     5   5
